newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower as yen rise hurts exporters.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower as yen rise hurts exporters.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower on Thursday as the yen's rapid advance against the dollar clouded prospects for export-driven issues, brokers said.

The weak sentiment was further hurt by the news that Tokyo prosecutors had raided Nomura Securities Co Ltd's headquarters as part of an investigation into suspected illegal payoffs, raising concerns about other brokerages, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average gave up 153.41 points or 0.76 percent to close at 20,056.31, off an earlier low of 19,854.99. Its June futures fell 180 points to 20,060.
Other major retreating sectors were precision instruments, rubber, sea transport and automobiles.
The stronger yen hurt recent leading issues such as Sony Corp, which fell 80 yen to 9,750, and Honda Motor Co Ltd, down 70 yen at 3,710.
Gaining sectors were led by real estate, communications, services, railway/bus, and transport equipment.
Hopes that urban land prices had bottomed out lifted real estate 0#REA.T shares.
The National Land Agency said it will announce its views on land prices on Friday at 0400 GMT.
"Since the yen's rise was sharp, we needed to wait and see for a while," said Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.
"If the dollar slides below 115.00 yen, where many companies set their (dollar/yen) internal rate, it would totally turn sentiment bearish," he said.
The U.S. currency slipped briefly past 116 yen to 115.60 during Tokyo trading hours, from its close of 117.30/40 yen on Wednesday in New York.
First section turnover was 423 million shares, against Wednesday's 421 million shares.
Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd rose 30 yen to 1,500. It briefly hit a high for this calendar year of 1,510.

Market participants are likely to pay close attention to currency movements for the time being, but if the yen stabilises against the dollar again, the Nikkei 225 would be supported at around 19,000, brokers said.
The second section index was up 3.80 points at 1,728.34, with 10.34 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 3.92 points at 1,177.99.
